faq.a: Abdulkadir is associated with the Arabic form عَبْدُ الْقَادِر, whose core sense is abdulkadir; servant of the capable.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulkadir?
faq.a: Abdulkadir is associated with Arabic. Abdulkadir is Arabic عَبْدُ الْقَادِر (ʿAbd al-Qādir), meaning 'servant of the Capable'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ الْقَادِر is Arabic.
Abdulkadir can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdulkadir should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd al-Qādir is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Abdulkadir mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Abdulkadir is rendered عبدالقادر and carries the sense عبدالقادر، بنده قادر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ab-dul-ka-dir. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.
